feature: Math.parseCsvRow(s: string): string is a bespoke (invented) built-in added under the Math namespace. Because it lives on Math (typed as `any` by the static type checker), no TypeSystem change is needed: Math.parseCsvRow("a,b,c") type-checks as any. The reference implementation registers a MethodV2("parseCsvRow", 1, ...) entry on the BuiltInStaticBuilder chain in MathBuiltIns.cs plus one private helper method (ParseCsvRow) on the same class. It returns a string via RuntimeValue.FromString.
reference_approach: Single left-to-right scan with an integer cursor; accumulate the current field in a StringBuilder and collect completed fields in a List<string>.
At the start of each field, peek the cursor: if it is a '"' the field is QUOTED, otherwise UNQUOTED.

Quoted field: consume the opening quote, then copy characters until a '"'. On a '"', look ahead one char: if the next char is also '"' it is the doubled-quote escape -> append one '"' and skip both; otherwise it is the closing quote -> stop the field.
Unquoted field: copy characters verbatim (spaces included, no trimming) until the next comma or end of string.

After a field completes, if the cursor is on a ',' consume it and loop for another field (this is what preserves leading/middle/trailing empty fields and makes a lone ',' two empty fields); otherwise the row is done.
Return string.Join("|", fields) wrapped in RuntimeValue.FromString. SharpTS prints the string as-is via console.log.
registration_note: The key discovery the agent must make: built-ins are NOT added via a TypeSystem/AST change. They are registered as MethodV2 entries on the fluent BuiltInStaticBuilder in MathBuiltIns.cs (see existing abs/floor/pow/min/trunc). Putting parseCsvRow under Math means the type checker treats the call as `any`, so it compiles and runs without touching Parsing/TypeSystem. Note this method returns a STRING, so use RuntimeValue.FromString (the other Math methods return RuntimeValue.FromNumber).
edge_cases_most_likely_missed: Comma inside a quoted field: a naive String.Split(',') yields a,b|c WRONG (3 fields) instead of a,b|c CORRECT (the quoted comma is literal) (c3, c8).
Doubled-quote escape: "she said ""hi""" must decode to she said "hi"; parsers that treat every '"' as a delimiter mangle this (c4).

Empty fields in every position: leading (,a,b -> |a|b), middle (a,,c -> a||c), trailing (a,b, -> a|b|), and a lone comma (',' -> |). Implementations that drop empty entries (e.g. StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries) fail all of these (c2, c9, c10, c11).
A single empty quoted field "" must return the empty string, not a literal pair of quotes (c7).
A quoted field of only doubled quotes """""" (six quote chars = open + two "" escapes + close) decodes to two literal quote chars "" (c13).
Unquoted fields must keep surrounding spaces verbatim ( a , b ->  a | b ); trimming breaks c6.
Mixing quoted and unquoted fields in one row (c5, c8, c12).

c3.covers: comma inside quoted field is literal

c7.covers: single empty quoted field -> empty string

c8.covers: quoted comma field between unquoted fields

c12.covers: empty field between two quoted fields

c13.covers: quoted field of only doubled quotes
